B.explanation: Total charge is $+2/3 -1/3 -1/3 = 0$, so it gives a neutral three-quark hadron.

C.explanation: Total charge is $+2/3 +2/3 -1/3 = +1e$, which is the proton composition, not neutral.

D.explanation: Total charge is $+2/3 +2/3 -1/3 = +1e$, so it cannot have zero charge.

hints: Notice the hadron contains three quarks, so add the three separate quark charges to get the total hadron charge which must equal zero.
Recall the quark charges in units of $e$: up is $+2/3$ while both down and strange are $-1/3$.
Test the sum $+2/3 -1/3 -1/3$ for the up-down-strange combination and compare it with the $+1e$ or $-1e$ sums of the other combinations.
walkthrough: A hadron made of three quarks is a baryon, so its charge is the algebraic sum of the three quark charges and must equal zero here.
Use the quark charges: up quark $+2/3e$, down quark $-1/3e$, strange quark $-1/3e$.
For the combination up, down, strange, the sum is $+2/3e -1/3e -1/3e = 0$.
For the other combinations, down-down-strange gives $-1e$ and both up-up-down and up-up-strange give $+2/3e +2/3e -1/3e = +1e$, so they are charged.
Only the up, down, strange combination gives zero total charge. This is option B
